title: Trumpet solos on records and Armstrong featuring Whitlock in Louisville
summary: Armstrong rarely featured other trumpeters on records, but at dances he featured Stump Whitlock, especially in Whitlock's hometown of Louisville.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: On the records, did you play the trumpet solos, other than Louis? Or did Ellis Whitlock? There's some trumpet in the background, and then -- of course, in 'High Society', I think that's you playing in the lead, in that one part where the saxes are playing the --
Well, Louis -- now, playing in the recordings, to be perfectly they played with the Frank, Recording, Louis didn't feature too many trumpeters.
But these weren't feature spots so much as they were --
But during the dance, he would feature. But, now, he featured Whitlock quite a bit, especially when Whitlock played his horn, sometimes. We played Louisville, Kentucky, I think.
Yes, uh-huh. So we played his home, and Louis featured him, because everybody was out, and they'd see Stumpy Stuffy sitting up there, and Louis featured him quite a bit.
Do you remember where you played in Louisville?
Unfortunately, I do not, because we were just in there for one night, and right out again.
